meta.description: Evidence-first canonical cybercrime knowledge base backed by Tier 1 Indian Government Authorities and official security advisories.

records.canonicalName: Digital Arrest & Fake Law Enforcement Video Call Extortion
records.summary: Organized cybercrime syndicates place IVR calls and WhatsApp/Skype video calls while impersonating CBI, Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB), ED, or Police, alleging illegal parcels or money laundering to force victims into continuous 'Digital Arrest' and extort funds.
records.executiveSummary: Cybercriminals set up artificial police studio backdrops and dress in official uniforms to conduct mock video interrogations. Victims are issued forged Supreme Court directives or arrest warrants and threatened with immediate imprisonment unless they transfer funds to 'Government Verification Accounts'.
howItWorks: Victim receives an automated IVR call claiming an international courier parcel containing illegal narcotics or passports in their name was seized.
Call is transferred to a fake police officer on WhatsApp/Skype video wearing official uniforms in a police station backdrop.
Scammer issues forged legal warrants and orders victim to remain on continuous camera presence ('Digital Arrest').
Victim is coerced into liquidating bank deposits into scammer-controlled 'RBI Escrow Verification Accounts'.
attackFlow: Coerced Fund Transfer to Mule Accounts
warningSigns: Demands to stay on continuous video call under 'Digital Arrest'
Calls originating from WhatsApp or Skype posing as law enforcement
Threats of immediate arrest unless funds are transferred for verification
Fake Supreme Court or CBI notices sent via messaging apps

callFormats: WhatsApp Video Accounts with Police Logos

records.victimImpact: Severe psychological distress, isolation, and extortion of life savings.
immediateActions: Disconnect the video call immediately; do NOT panic
Do NOT transfer any money for court or police verification
Report the incident immediately to 1930 Cyber Crime Helpline
Lodge a complaint on cybercrime.gov.in
prevention: Remember: THERE IS NO LEGAL CONCEPT OF 'DIGITAL ARREST' IN INDIAN LAW
Police, CBI, ED, and Customs NEVER conduct interrogations or arrests over video calls
Official police notices under Section 41A CrPC are issued physically, never via WhatsApp
records.reportingGuidance: File a report under 'Report Cyber Crime' on cybercrime.gov.in and inform local police station.
records.officialGuidance: I4C (MHA) National Advisory: Disconnect suspicious video calls immediately and report on 1930 Helpline.

sources.title: National Advisory on Digital Arrest Extortion

records.canonicalName: Fake Police Accusation & Emergency Family Bail Money Scam
records.summary: Scammers call parents claiming their child or family member has been detained by police in a serious accident or crime, demanding instant cash or UPI transfer for emergency bail.
records.executiveSummary: Fraudsters exploit parental anxiety by placing unexpected phone calls claiming a relative is in police custody. Background audio of crying is often played while demanding instant funds before an FIR is lodged.
howItWorks: Parent receives an urgent call claiming their son/daughter was caught in a road accident or crime.
Scammer plays fake background crying audio pretending to be the victim.
Scammer demands ₹25,000 to ₹1,00,000 via UPI to prevent formal arrest.
attackFlow: Demand for Instant UPI Bail Transfer
warningSigns: High-pressure calls causing immediate panic about family safety
Demand for instant UPI transfer to drop charges
Caller refusing to let victim speak directly on phone
records.victimImpact: Instant loss of funds driven by emotional manipulation.
immediateActions: Call your child/relative directly on their personal phone number to confirm safety
Ask the caller for their police station name and verify with local police
Report caller number to 1930 Helpline and cybercrime.gov.in
prevention: Police NEVER accept bail money via UPI or personal money transfer
Always verify family safety independently before reacting to urgent calls
records.reportingGuidance: Report caller number to 1930 Helpline and local police station.
records.officialGuidance: I4C (MHA) Public Advisory: Verify caller identity independently and report emergency impersonation fraud on 1930.

records.canonicalName: UPI Collect Request & Malicious QR Code Payment Fraud
records.summary: Scammers send UPI Collect Requests or QR codes disguised as refunds or advance buyer payments, tricking victims into entering their UPI PIN under the false belief that PIN is needed to receive money.
records.executiveSummary: Cybercriminals abuse the 'Collect VPA' function of UPI apps or send phishing QR images. They exploit common confusion regarding payment direction to debit funds instantly when victims enter their 4/6-digit PIN.
howItWorks: Scammer contacts seller on marketplace (OLX/Quikr) agreeing to buy an item instantly.
Scammer sends a QR code or UPI Collect Request over WhatsApp claiming 'Scan/Approve to receive payment'.
Victim enters UPI PIN believing funds will be credited.
Account is debited immediately.
attackFlow: UPI Collect Request / QR Code Sent
warningSigns: Insistence that entering UPI PIN is required to RECEIVE money
UPI app notification stating 'Pay ₹X' instead of 'Received ₹X'
Unsolicited QR codes sent for rewards or cashback
immediateActions: Block the scammer's UPI VPA in your payment app
Report fraudulent transaction to bank support and 1930 Helpline
File complaint on cybercrime.gov.in
prevention: GOLDEN RULE: UPI PIN is ONLY required for SENDING money, NEVER for receiving money
Receiving money requires ZERO action on your part; it credits automatically
Never scan QR codes to receive money
records.reportingGuidance: Report fraud VPA to bank app and 1930 National Cyber Helpline.
records.officialGuidance: NPCI Operational Safety Directive: Entering UPI PIN is strictly required only to send money.

records.canonicalName: Fake Bank Account Freeze & KYC Phishing Scam
records.summary: Scammers impersonate bank officials or telecom providers via SMS and calls, claiming account or SIM block due to expired KYC, directing victims to phishing portals to capture NetBanking credentials.
records.executiveSummary: Cybercriminals send bulk SMS with spoofed headers threatening account suspension within hours. Links lead to cloned bank NetBanking sites that harvest Customer IDs, passwords, and OTPs in real-time.
howItWorks: Victim receives SMS: 'Your bank account will be blocked today due to pending KYC. Update at link'.
Phishing link opens a fake bank login interface.
Victim enters NetBanking User ID, password, and incoming OTP.
Scammers execute real-time IMPS/NEFT transfers draining account.
warningSigns: SMS sent from 10-digit personal numbers instead of official bank headers
Urgent threats of account block within 2-24 hours
Websites asking for NetBanking password or CVV
records.victimImpact: Total account compromise and unauthorized wire transfers.
immediateActions: Call bank helpline immediately to freeze NetBanking and debit cards
Call 1930 Helpline within the 2-hour Golden Window
Report phishing URL on cybercrime.gov.in
prevention: Banks NEVER ask for passwords, PINs, or OTPs over phone or SMS
Log in to NetBanking ONLY by typing the official bank URL directly into browser
Check official SMS sender headers (e.g. AD-SBIINB)
records.reportingGuidance: Report compromised accounts to 1930 and bank cyber incident team.
records.officialGuidance: RBI Public Protection Advisory: Never click SMS links regarding bank account block.

records.summary: Scammers initiate unauthorized financial transactions or account resets and trick victims into revealing the incoming OTP under pretexts of delivery confirmation or accidental SMS transfers.
records.executiveSummary: Fraudsters manipulate victims into sharing One-Time Passwords by posing as delivery agents or customer care representatives. Once obtained, the OTP authorizes unauthorized debits or account takeovers.
howItWorks: Scammer initiates an online card transaction or app login using victim's phone number.
Scammer calls victim claiming to be a delivery executive needing OTP for package drop.
Victim reads OTP out loud; scammer completes transaction.
warningSigns: Unsolicited calls asking for 6-digit SMS verification codes
OTP SMS explicitly warning 'Do NOT share this code'
Receiving OTPs when you did not initiate any action
immediateActions: Call bank helpline immediately to block card/account
Report incident to 1930 Helpline and cybercrime.gov.in
prevention: NEVER share OTPs with anyone—including bank staff or delivery agents
Always read the exact text inside OTP SMS specifying amount and merchant
records.reportingGuidance: Report fraud to 1930 Helpline and bank customer care.
records.officialGuidance: CERT-In Security Advisory: Keep OTPs strictly confidential.

records.canonicalName: Work From Home & Telegram Prepaid Task Recruitment Scam
records.summary: Scammers send unsolicited job offers promising high daily earnings for liking YouTube videos or writing reviews, luring victims into Telegram groups that demand tiered prepaid deposits for VIP tasks.
records.executiveSummary: Fraudsters recruit victims via WhatsApp/SMS for simple online tasks. Small initial payouts are made to build trust, after which victims are pressured into depositing large sums for 'VIP Investment Tasks' that block withdrawals.
howItWorks: SMS/WhatsApp received offering ₹3,000/day for online rating tasks.
Victim completes initial tasks and receives ₹150-₹300 trust payout.
Victim added to Telegram VIP channel requiring ₹5,000 to ₹2,00,000 prepaid deposits.
Withdrawal is blocked; admins demand additional 'taxes'.
warningSigns: Job offers promising high income for trivial video-liking tasks
Requirement to deposit money before withdrawing earned wages
Recruitment conducted entirely via anonymous Telegram groups
records.victimImpact: Substantial financial loss across multiple deposit tiers.
immediateActions: Stop making further prepaid task deposits immediately
Preserve chat exports and UPI transaction UTR numbers
File complaint at 1930 Helpline and cybercrime.gov.in
prevention: Legitimate companies NEVER charge job seekers fees or demand prepaid task deposits
Verify corporate job offers on official company career portals
records.reportingGuidance: Lodge report on cybercrime.gov.in under Online Financial Fraud.
records.officialGuidance: I4C (MHA) Advisory: Beware of part-time task scams operating on messaging apps.

sources.title: Advisory on Part-Time Task Job Fraud

records.canonicalName: Illegal Instant Loan App Extortion & Photo Morphing Racket
records.summary: Unauthorized instant loan APK apps trap borrowers with easy micro-loans, secretly exfiltrate phone contact lists and gallery photos, and resort to photo morphing blackmail and contact harassment.
records.executiveSummary: Unapproved loan apps offer quick funds without documentation. Upon installation, the APK exfiltrates contacts and media. Recovery agents demand 300% interest within 7 days, threatening to broadcast morphed offensive images to all contacts.
howItWorks: Victim installs an unverified loan APK from web ad promising instant loan.
App exfiltrates full phone Contacts and Photo Gallery during setup.
App disburses partial loan amount and demands exorbitant repayment in 7 days.
If unpaid, recovery agents send morphed offensive photos to victim's contacts.
warningSigns: App not listed on Google Play Store or Apple App Store
Requests broad permissions to Contacts, Camera, and Storage
Repayment tenure under 60 days (violates RBI guidelines)
records.victimImpact: Severe social humiliation and continuous extortion.
immediateActions: Revoke app permissions and uninstall loan APK file immediately
Inform contacts about the data breach / harassment
File complaint at 1930 Helpline and cybercrime.gov.in
prevention: Borrow ONLY from RBI-registered banks and NBFCs listed on RBI website
Never sideload APK files from web ads or unknown links
records.reportingGuidance: Report illegal loan app to RBI Sachet portal and 1930 Helpline.
records.officialGuidance: RBI Public Notice: Do not download illegal loan apps offering unauthorized credit.

sources.title: Advisory on Illegal Digital Lending Apps

records.canonicalName: Fake Stock Trading & SEBI Broker Impersonation Ponzi Scheme
records.summary: Fraudulent stock trading platforms impersonate reputed SEBI brokers, offering guaranteed high returns on equities or IPO allotments, luring victims into transferring money into private accounts.
records.executiveSummary: Scammers advertise stock trading courses on social media leading to VIP WhatsApp groups. Fake trading apps display artificial portfolio profits, but withdrawals are permanently blocked when victims attempt to Cash Out.
howItWorks: Victim joins 'Institutional Trading' WhatsApp group via web ads.
Fake stock tips and fabricated profit screenshots are posted by bots.
Victim deposits money into private accounts via custom trading app.
App shows fake profits; withdrawal requests demand additional 'tax fees'.
warningSigns: Guarantees of fixed high stock profits with zero risk
Investment money requested in individual personal bank accounts
Trading conducted on unverified custom apps not listed on SEBI/NSE
immediateActions: Stop depositing funds into trading portal immediately
Lodge complaint on SEBI SCORES portal, 1930 Helpline and cybercrime.gov.in
Report mule bank details to cybercrime.gov.in
prevention: Trade ONLY through SEBI-registered brokers verified on sebi.gov.in
Never deposit trading money into personal bank accounts
records.reportingGuidance: File complaint on SEBI SCORES portal (scores.gov.in) and 1930 Helpline.
records.officialGuidance: SEBI Advisory: Beware of unregistered entities offering guaranteed stock returns.

sources.title: SEBI Warning Against Unauthorized Trading Schemes

records.canonicalName: SIM Swap & Telecom Identity Hijacking Fraud
records.summary: Scammers trick telecom operators into issuing a duplicate SIM card for your phone number, cutting off your network connection and capturing all incoming banking OTPs.
records.executiveSummary: Fraudsters pose as telecom customer care offering 5G upgrades to trick victims into forwarding SIM card numbers or eSIM QR codes. Once activated, the scammer's SIM receives all banking SMS OTPs.
howItWorks: Scammer calls victim offering 'Free 5G SIM Upgrade'.
Tricks victim into sending 20-digit SIM number via SMS to operator.
Operator issues new SIM to scammer; victim's phone loses signal.
Scammer logs into victim's NetBanking using intercepted OTPs.
warningSigns: Sudden total loss of phone network signal in coverage area
Requests to SMS 20-digit SIM number or scan eSIM QR codes
Confirmation SMS from telecom operator regarding SIM swap
records.victimImpact: Complete interception of multi-factor authentication codes.
immediateActions: If signal disappears suddenly, contact mobile operator immediately from another phone
Block bank NetBanking & cards via bank helpline
Report to 1930 Helpline and cybercrime.gov.in
prevention: Operators NEVER ask customers to SMS SIM numbers for 5G upgrades
Never share eSIM activation QR codes
records.reportingGuidance: Report unauthorized SIM swap to telecom operator and 1930 Helpline.
records.officialGuidance: DoT Advisory: Guard SIM card details and report sudden network loss on 1930.

sources.title: DoT Advisory on SIM Swap Frauds

records.canonicalName: WhatsApp Account Takeover & Family Emergency Scam
records.summary: Scammers hijack a friend or relative's WhatsApp account and send urgent messages requesting emergency money transfers or trick victims into sharing verification PINs.
records.executiveSummary: By taking over a known contact's account, scammers exploit existing social trust. They send urgent distress messages requesting money transfers via UPI for medical or legal emergencies.
howItWorks: Scammer hijacks contact's WhatsApp account via verification code trick.
Messages victim: 'Emergency! Hospitalized, please send ₹20,000 via UPI'.
Victim transfers money believing it is their real friend.
warningSigns: Unexpected message from a contact asking for urgent money
Sender refusing to take a voice call claiming emergency
Requests asking you to forward 6-digit WhatsApp SMS codes
records.victimImpact: Financial loss driven by social trust exploitation.
immediateActions: Call contact on regular voice call to verify emergency independently
Report hijacked account in WhatsApp app settings
Call 1930 Helpline and report on cybercrime.gov.in if funds were sent
prevention: ALWAYS call contact on phone to verify before sending emergency money
Enable Two-Step Verification (6-digit PIN) in WhatsApp Settings
records.reportingGuidance: Report account hijacking to WhatsApp support and 1930 Helpline.
records.officialGuidance: CERT-In Security Note: Enable 2FA on instant messaging apps.

records.canonicalName: Screen Mirroring & Remote Access Software Fraud
records.summary: Scammers guide victims to install remote screen-sharing apps (AnyDesk, RustDesk, TeamViewer), allowing them to view phone screens live and capture banking PINs during transactions.
records.executiveSummary: Fraudsters posing as customer care trick victims into downloading remote access software. By viewing the phone screen live, scammers capture NetBanking passwords and UPI PINs as victims type them.
howItWorks: Victim calls fake customer care number found online for refund help.
Scammer instructs victim to install AnyDesk app from Play Store.
Scammer obtains 9-digit session code and views victim's screen live.
Scammer watches victim enter banking PIN and steals funds.
warningSigns: Customer support agent demanding installation of AnyDesk or RustDesk
Request to share a 9-digit app session code
Screen notice displaying 'Someone can see your screen'
records.victimImpact: Complete live device screen exposure and banking compromise.
immediateActions: Turn off Wi-Fi/Mobile Data immediately or switch to Airplane Mode
Uninstall remote access software
Call bank helpline and 1930 Helpline to block accounts, report on cybercrime.gov.in
prevention: NEVER install remote control software on advice of phone callers
Banks and support teams NEVER require remote screen control
records.reportingGuidance: Report incident to 1930 Helpline and bank cyber fraud cell.
records.officialGuidance: RBI Warning: Do not grant remote access screen permissions to strangers.

sources.title: Advisory on Remote Access Application Risks

records.canonicalName: Video Call Blackmail & Online Sextortion Racket
records.summary: Victims receive unsolicited video calls from unknown profiles. Once accepted, scammers record screen footage with explicit clips and demand extortion money under threat of social media leaks.
records.executiveSummary: Cyber blackmailers initiate video calls showing pre-recorded explicit video while recording victim reactions. Edited clips are used to demand extortion money, often followed by fake police calls threatening arrest.
howItWorks: Unknown profile initiates video call on WhatsApp/Instagram.
Victim answers; screen displays explicit footage while recording victim's face.
Scammer threatens to send edited video to victim's Facebook contacts unless money is paid.
Fake 'Cyber Police Officer' calls demanding deletion fees.
warningSigns: Video calls from unknown female profiles on social media
Demands for money to prevent uploading video clips
Follow-up calls from fake police threatening arrest for porn charges
records.victimImpact: Severe psychological distress, fear, and financial extortion.
immediateActions: Do NOT pay money to blackmailers (paying leads to higher demands)
Block the blackmailer's number immediately
Report to 1930 Helpline and cybercrime.gov.in
prevention: NEVER answer video calls from unknown contacts on social media
Cover front camera when taking calls from unknown numbers
Set social media profiles to Private
records.reportingGuidance: Report under 'Report Cyber Crime' on cybercrime.gov.in and dial 1930.
records.officialGuidance: I4C (MHA) Advisory: Do not pay blackmailers; report sextortion to 1930.

records.canonicalName: Fake Cryptocurrency Exchange & Web3 DApp Mining Fraud
records.summary: Scammers build fake crypto trading platforms or liquidity mining Web3 dApps promising 10% daily USDT returns, obtaining unlimited token approvals to drain connected crypto wallets.
records.executiveSummary: Fraudsters target victims on social apps, guiding them to connect crypto wallets to malicious dApps. Phishing smart contracts request unlimited allowance approvals, allowing scammers to siphon all wallet tokens.
howItWorks: Victim lured via dating apps or social media into 'Liquidity Mining'.
Directed to connect Web3 wallet (MetaMask/Trust Wallet) to phishing dApp link.
Phishing smart contract grants scammer unlimited token approval.
All USDT/Crypto in wallet is drained automatically.
warningSigns: Promises of guaranteed daily percentage returns in cryptocurrency
Trading on unverified web exchanges instead of FIU-registered exchanges
Smart contract prompts requesting 'Unlimited Allowance Approval'
records.victimImpact: Total drain of Web3 crypto wallet balances.
immediateActions: Disconnect Web3 wallet from dApp immediately
Revoke token approvals using Etherscan/BscScan token approval tools
Report TxHashes on 1930 Helpline and cybercrime.gov.in
prevention: Trade ONLY on FIU-registered cryptocurrency exchanges in India
Never connect Web3 wallets to unverified web links
Regularly audit token approvals
records.reportingGuidance: Report crypto fraud details to 1930 Helpline and cybercrime.gov.in.
records.officialGuidance: CERT-In Security Bulletin: Guard Web3 wallet approvals and avoid unverified exchanges.

sources.title: Advisory on Web3 Crypto Wallet Security

records.canonicalName: Google Search & Maps Fake Customer Care Helpline Fraud
records.summary: Scammers edit public Google Maps listings and publish SEO-optimized fake posts containing mobile numbers listed as 24x7 customer support for banks, airlines, or e-commerce, looting callers seeking refunds.
records.executiveSummary: Cybercriminals publish fake helpline numbers for popular brands online. When victims call for refund help, scammers guide them to scan QR codes or install remote access software to steal banking credentials.
howItWorks: Victim searches Google for bank or courier customer helpline number.
Finds a sponsored ad or edited map listing displaying scammer's 10-digit number.
Victim calls number; scammer claims 'To process refund, scan QR or download AnyDesk'.
Scammer steals funds.
warningSigns: Customer support number starting with regular mobile digits (+91 9XXXX) instead of 1800 toll-free
Helpline agent asking to install remote control software
Asking for UPI PIN to process a refund

technicalIndicators.vector: SEO Search Engine Poisoning & Edited Maps Profile

records.victimImpact: Loss of bank funds during refund seeking.
immediateActions: Call actual bank helpline (from back of debit card) to block cards
Report fake helpline number to 1930 Helpline and cybercrime.gov.in
prevention: NEVER trust customer care numbers found on Google Search or Maps
ALWAYS obtain support numbers ONLY from inside official mobile apps or official websites
records.reportingGuidance: Report fake listing to 1930 Helpline and search engine feedback.
records.officialGuidance: RBI Public Advisory: Do not call unverified customer care numbers found on search engines.

sources.title: Advisory on Fake Helpline Number Scams
